name_reason: Compliant: correct data_fd2_battle_ prefix (battle core read-only table), descriptive (main 12-sprite summon-spell animation y-offset), reflects data type (table/array). The '12' is a legitimate domain dimension (12 sprites/slots, indexed 0..11 by the per-slot color index that the consumer initializes to the slot index), not a Ghidra address residue. No address-derived suffix. Minor stylistic nuance: siblings at 0x52490/0x5249C use '12color' since all three are indexed by the same color index; '12slot' here is still accurate and not worth churning.
purpose: Per-color baseline vertical pixel offset for the 12 sprites of the main summon-spell (召喚系) animation.
logic_summary: Read-only base offset table. Sole reader fd2_tick_summon_spell_main_animation_state (@ 0x26795) copies the whole 12-dword table into a stack-local int[12] (12-iteration dword copy, stride 4), applies a +0x14 baseline shift to every entry when the caster is on the enemy team (bTeam==0), then per visible slot computes screen y = origin_y + y_offset[color_idx] - v_offset[color_idx]*row_stride and blits the sprite. color_idx is the per-slot color index array (init to slot index, rotates mod 12).
element_semantics: Signed vertical pixel offset (int32) for sprite color index 0..11; values include negatives (-30, -10), so element is signed. Indexed by the per-slot color index. Values (LE) = {30,0,70,40,130,70,-30,30,110,80,-10,30}.
notes: Memory @ 0x52460 (48 bytes) = 12 int32 LE {30,0,70,40,130,70,-30,30,110,80,-10,30}, byte-identical to the src initializer. Only xrefs are READs at 0x267b9 (DATA addr-load) / 0x267be in fd2_tick_summon_spell_main_animation_state; no writers => const confirmed. Consumer's 12-iter dword copy loop (int* src/dst) + signed entries fix int32[12] (matches Ghidra int[12]). src comment was already accurate and precise (kept). Ghidra data plate (PLATE_COMMENT @ 0x52460) was blank; created a concise plate via run_script_inline reflecting the src conclusion. src/table/btltab2.c not edited (comment kept), so only the shard is staged.
